references.text: The preceding verse provides the context for how the Passover lamb is to be eaten—with unleavened bread and bitter herbs—and specifies that it must be roasted over fire.
Further instructions regarding the Passover lamb, including that it must be eaten in one house and that no bones are to be broken.
Reiterates the command to roast and eat the Passover offering, linking it to the celebration at the place the Lord chooses.
Describes how the Passover lamb was roasted over fire in accordance with the regulation during King Josiah's Passover celebration.
Instructions for the second Passover observance, which include eating the lamb with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
Ritual parallel: Both verses define fire as the only acceptable means of handling holy offerings (either through roasting or complete burning).
Ritual parallel: Both verses prohibit consuming food before a specific offering has been performed and emphasize the importance of correct ritual handling (roasting/preparation) in sacred contexts.
